title: Pilot check-in: SLO variance and graceful degradation plan
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recurring tail-latency and intermittent 5xx/timeouts observed under mid-size bursts. We reviewed client retry behavior, server-side rate windows, and KV cache warmup impacts; agreed on a set of experiments (traffic-shaping, adaptive backoff, reduced concurrency for cold KV paths) and identified telemetry gaps to close for root-cause analysis.
action_items: Ravi Patel - run staged load test (50/100/200 rps) with trace-level logging and KV cache metrics exported; deliver logs and flamegraphs by 2027-05-07
Aisha Gomez - share recent prod-ish request traces and one failing sample (raw payload) by 2027-05-05
Tom Bradford - provision a VPC peering test env and confirm egress rules for TLS/KMS traffic by 2027-05-10
Maya Chen - send updated fallback policy doc (canary thresholds + weighted fallback) and pricing delta for Dedicated nodes by 2027-05-06
Lena Ortiz - finalize success criteria for pilot (p95/p99 targets, max acceptable error rate) and circulate to stakeholders by 2027-05-06
next_steps: Redwood to run warmup experiment to measure KV cache miss tail latency and report 95/99 latencies
Customer to test reduced client retry budget and exponential backoff with jitter on non-idempotent calls
Schedule 1:1 deep-dive if backend traces show heavy GC or serialization stalls
Follow-up call scheduled for 2027-05-11 16:00 UTC to review results
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Lead ML Engineer, Cascadia), Tom Bradford (Platform Eng, Cascadia), Lena Ortiz (Product)

Automated summary (may be partial): recurring tail latency and intermittent 5xxs during mid-size bursts; discuss retry budgets, rate-windowing, KV cache warmup impact, telemetry gaps.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we got about 50 minutes on the calendar. Quick check, is this still a good time?
[00:08] Aisha: Yep, good here, thanks.
[00:12] Tom: All set.
[00:15] Maya: Cool. Ravi you'll lead the technical bits, I'll cover rollout/fallback options and pricing notes.
[00:22] Ravi: Yep, I'll jump in. So quick recaps from your side Aisha — you mentioned p99 spikes around 2-3x higher on Tuesdays during the campaign load? Can you restate the pattern?
[00:32] Aisha: Uh yeah, so most of our normal traffic has p95 around 120ms, p99 around 480. On campaign Tuesdays when there's a surge, p99 goes to 1.2 to 1.6s intermittently, and we also see about 0.3% 5xx — mostly timeouts and occasionally a 502 proxy.
[00:48] Lena: The spike aligns with our batch personalization job and external images fetch so there's a mixed IO pattern.
[00:55] Tom: We've got some fanout to image service which is outside Redwood, but the majority of tokens are coming from the personalization LLM prompt.
[01:05] Ravi: Got it. Two quick things to confirm: are you using any client-side retry library with default retries? And are you routing through a VPC peered egress or public internet?
[01:15] Aisha: We use a homegrown retry layer; default 3 retries for 5xx and timeouts, exponential backoff but no jitter. We're on a VPC peering for the pilot with NAT gateway for outside calls.
[01:28] Ravi: No jitter is notable — jitter helps avoid synchronized retries causing a thundering herd.
[01:32] Maya: Also we saw that your sample traces show many initial requests hitting a cold KV cache path — lots of prefix misses. That amplifies tail latencies for first tokens.
[01:44] Aisha: We suspected KV cache cold starts, but didn't have fine-grained metrics to prove it.
[01:50] Ravi: Right. The plan we propose: first, run a warmup workload focused on prefix-cache population then measure p99 with a smaller concurrency to isolate cache effect. Second, tune the client retry budget down for non-idempotent calls and add randomized jitter. Third, add a short-term graceful-deg path where fallback model with lower context/quantized profile is used when latency thresholds breach.
[02:18] Tom: Can you explain the fallback model cost/quality tradeoff again? We worry about user experience if fallback produces lower-quality completions.
[02:26] Maya: Sure — fallback is not intended as permanent; it's a degraded mode where, for example, we route to a lower-parameter variant or a more aggressively quantized binary with a smaller KV cache footprint. It cuts median latency and reduces tail at cost of occasional quality drop. We recommend weighted routing with canary and user-visible disclaimers only for specific flows.
[02:44] Lena: Okay. We have strict SLOs for checkout path, so fallback can't be used there. But for personalization widgets it's acceptable.
[02:52] Ravi: Good distinction. For checkout we should prioritize retries with backoff and client-side circuit breaker to open on rate-window saturation. For non-critical widgets we can enable the fallback.
[03:04] Aisha: About rate-windowing — our platform saw spikes in 429s last week and we observed the Redwood rate-window was triggering transiently. Any suggestions on smoothing?
[03:14] Maya: We can adjust server-side rate windowing: longer window, token-bucket smoothing, and burst allowance. Also we can prioritize requests by route — e.g., checkout route gets higher weight.
[03:25] Ravi: Another operational knob is dynamic concurrency per model shard; we can reduce max concurrency for shards that show KV cache misses to avoid long queues. That trades throughput for tail.
[03:36] Tom: How does the KV cache eviction behave on Dedicated nodes vs Hosted? We might move to Dedicated but want to understand hot-key behavior.
[03:44] Ravi: On Dedicated you can increase cache residency and pin prefixes for a tenant; Hosted has multi-tenant LRU tuned globally. If you pin prefixes on Dedicated, tail due to cold misses drops significantly. There is a cost/ops tradeoff.
[03:56] Aisha: We asked about KMS/HSM for key management — any blockers with peered VPCs?
[04:02] Maya: No blockers — we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations. Egress rules need to allow TLS to the KMS endpoints; we'll provide a network checklist.
[04:11] Tom: Good. On telemetry, we only have coarse p95/p99 at the route level; not per-token or KV cache-level metrics. That makes RCA painful.
[04:20] Ravi: That's a big gap. We'll share a small instrumentation patch that emits KV cache hit/miss counters, per-request tokenization timing, and end-to-end trace IDs. That will help correlate stalls with serialization or GPU stalls.
[04:34] Lena: Perfect — we'll try to instrument next week.
[04:38] Maya: Let's talk about retries and idempotency. Since many calls are non-idempotent, we recommended reducing retries to 1 and using exponential backoff with jitter, and for read-only generation you can keep 2 retries.
[04:52] Aisha: Our current 3 retries without jitter probably amplified the issue during the surge.
[04:57] Ravi: Exactly. Also implement client-side circuit breaker: if you see a burst of 5xx/429 in a short window, open for a configurable cool-down and route to fallback.
[05:07] Tom: On the server we saw occasional 502s coming from the edge proxy under load — are those coming from upstream timeouts or internal queue saturation?
[05:16] Ravi: In prior traces we saw a mix. Some 502s were from head-of-line blocking where a long-running decode stalled a worker and queued bolus of requests. The runtime supports preemption and work-stealing but long KV miss paths can still cause head-of-line effects.
[05:33] Aisha: Any immediate mitigation for that?
[05:36] Ravi: Short-term: reduce max concurrency on the shard, increase worker parallelism, add per-request CPU/bundle limits, and ramp up canary fallback for that route during observed spike windows. Longer-term, we can improve KV cache async prefetch and warmup.
[05:51] Maya: We'll propose a concrete test matrix this week: baseline, warmup, reduced retries, fallback enabled, and Dedicated-configured pinning (if you want to try Dedicated).
[05:59] Lena: About Dedicated — what's the lead time and minimum commitment?
[06:04] Maya: Typical lead time is 2–4 weeks after contract; minimum is a monthly reservation for a node pool. I'll send pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[06:12] Tom: Back to telemetry — what format will Redwood provide traces in? We use Zipkin/Jaeger currently.
[06:18] Ravi: We can emit Jaeger spans and open telemetry. We'll also provide a CSV export for p95/p99 windows and raw token timing if you prefer.
[06:28] Aisha: That helps. One more thing — we saw a regression when we enabled a larger context window; tokenization time shot up and some requests timed out. Could quantization profiles help there?
[06:39] Ravi: Yes — higher context increases KV lookups and attention compute; lighter quantization reduces memory bandwidth but may slightly impact quality. For context-heavy flows, try a quantized model with 8-bit kernels optimized for long sequences; that often narrows the tail. We'll share recommended quantization profiles per model.
[06:58] Lena: Are there tradeoffs with coherency of embeddings or rerank quality if we quantize?
[07:04] Ravi: Slight differences at edge cases — we'll run prompt-preservation tests as part of the experiment. If it fails, fallback remains an option.
[07:12] Maya: Alright — let's walk through the experiment schedule. Ravi?
[07:18] Ravi: Plan A (this week): run a cold-start warmup — 5k warmup requests over 10 minutes to populate KV prefixes, then a steady-state burst at 100 rps for 10 minutes to capture p95/99. Instrument with traces. Plan B: reduce client retries + jitter and re-run. Plan C: enable fallback to quantized model (canary at 5%) and measure error/quality delta. We'll run these in parallel in a staging environment and share dashboards.
[07:45] Tom: For the warmup, do we need to change anything on our side?
[07:49] Ravi: Just trigger a replay of representative prompts; we'll provide a replay harness. If you can't share full data, you can anonymize but keep token distributions.
[07:58] Aisha: We'll get a sample of prompts and share a sanitized set by Thursday.
[08:04] Lena: About the dashboards, can we get per-route p99 and KV cache hit rate?
[08:09] Maya: Yes, we'll add KV hit/miss and per-route tail plots to the pilot dashboard.
[08:14] Aisha: What about security — we need SOC2 in the procurement thread; do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO?
[08:21] Maya: We are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. I'll attach the security pack and the network checklist.
[08:29] Tom: SSO and SAML integration for our ops team?
[08:32] Maya: Supported — SAML SSO, RBAC, enterprise audit logs. We'll share the integration guide.
[08:38] Ravi: Quick note — if you plan Dedicated, you can enable VPC-only control plane. That avoids public egress for control traffic.
[08:45] Tom: Sounds good.
[08:47] Aisha: One question on billing — if we run warmups and extra experiments, how does Redwood meter that?
[08:54] Maya: Warmup traffic in pilot is included within a testing allowance for POC; we'll flag large-scale stress tests as out-of-scope and discuss capacity credits. I'll specify in follow-up.
[09:03] Ravi: We're going to instrument more detailed per-request timing; expect some added logs which may push storage. We'll compress and keep retention short for the test window.
[09:12] Lena: Fine.
[09:14] Maya: Any blockers on the action items?
[09:17] Tom: None at the moment. We'll start the VPC peering checklist.
[09:21] Aisha: We'll prepare sample prompts and traces.
[09:24] Ravi: Great. Quick note on retry budget math: with your current 3 retries, worst-case fanout multiplies requests up to 4x. If you reduce to 1 retry and add jitter, that should significantly reduce pressure.
[09:38] Aisha: Understood. We'll prototype the client changes in staging.
[09:41] Maya: Ok time check — about 40 minutes left, but I think the major decisions are here. Any deep technical dig needed?
[09:48] Tom: We might want a 1:1 SE session to unpack traces if the initial instrumentation shows surprising GC stalls.
[09:54] Ravi: Yep, happy to do a deep-dive — we can schedule a trace triage session.
[09:58] Lena: Let's do that if needed.
[10:01] Maya: Final recap: Redwood will send fallback policy doc, network checklist, pricing tiers, and instrumentation patch. Customer will send sanitized traces, provision VPC peering, and change client-level retry/jitter. We'll run warmup/load experiments and meet back on 2027-05-11 to review.
[10:20] Aisha: Sounds good. Thank you.
[10:23] Tom: Thanks all.
[10:25] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and next steps.
[51:30] (call ends)
